The search didn't turn up an NREL line-item breakdown of two-tank molten salt storage costs by tanks, pumps, and heat exchangers in $/kWh. It did surface related figures and a few component notes.

- **NREL cost model:** NREL's Molten Salt Power Tower Cost Model for SAM is a two-tank, direct-storage reference design with a spreadsheet for estimating costs at different plant sizes. The spreadsheet allows users to estimate the costs of different-size plants and to take into account changes in commodity prices. The search didn't show its per-component breakdown, so you'll need the report itself (NREL/TP-5500-57625) and its spreadsheet at sam.nrel.gov/cost.
- **Pumps and exchangers:** A separate study of carbonate-salt two-tank systems notes that salt pumps and, for indirect storage, an additional heat exchanger add significant cost to the system.
- **Cost range:** A 2004 two-tank parabolic trough study estimated the specific cost for a two-tank molten salt storage is in the range of US$ 30–40/kWhth depending on storage size.
- **Chloride salts:** A 2021 NREL paper on molten chloride storage estimated the cost of the TES system is estimated to be $60/kWhth, which is four times greater than Department of Energy targets.

Search results give a few 2025 figures, but none is a clean U.S. utility-scale installed-cost benchmark.

- **Ember (October 2025):** Outside the U.S. and China, the all-in capex for a long-duration utility-scale project is around $125/kWh, comprising $75/kWh for the core equipment shipped from China and around $50/kWh for installation and grid connection. Ember's figures come from auction results in Saudi Arabia, India and Italy, plus expert interviews (interviews conducted by Ember in October 2025). Ember also says some auctions even suggest capex below $100/kWh, though it attributes those cases to developer expectations of future battery prices.
- **BloombergNEF via Volta:** Turnkey BESS costs fell another 31% from 2024 to 2025, at $117/kWh, a number reached by weighting the global averages. The same source notes that costs in China are as low as $63/kWh when compared to Europe's $120/kWh.
- **Benchmark Mineral Intelligence:** Chinese project tenders fell to as low as $63/kWh in 2025. Early 2026 brought a reversal, with lithium prices at a two-year high and 314Ah ESS LFP cell prices rising by approximately 10% from recent lows.
- **Ember on BNEF's core-equipment benchmark:** BNEF's 2024 global core-equipment figure was around $165/kWh, but this figure averages higher-cost markets such as the U.S. and a wider supplier base.

The U.S. figure is the gap. NREL's ATB material says installed $/kWh costs decrease with duration, but the snippet gives no 2025 value, so a U.S. utility-scale number would need a separate search (for example, NREL's 2025 ATB or Lazard).

content.text:
## Building it from the bottom up

**Step 1 — how much salt do you actually need?**

Solar salt (60% NaNO₃ / 40% KNO₃), Cp ≈ 1.5 kJ/kg·K, operated across a ~275°C ΔT (cold tank ~290°C, hot tank ~565°C):

m = E/(Cp·ΔT) = 18,000,000 kJ / (1.5 × 275) ≈ 43,600 kg (~44 t), say 50 t with ullage/heel margin.

At ~$1,000/t bulk nitrate salt, that's **~$50,000** — essentially a rounding error on the total system. This is the first key insight: at small scale the storage *medium* is never the cost driver. The cost is the infrastructure needed to contain, move, and heat-trace 24 m³ of salt that freezes solid below ~220°C.

**Step 2 — the balance-of-plant, which actually sets the price**

| Component | Basis | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Salt + heel margin | 50 t @ ~$1,000/t | $50k |
| Hot tank (SS, insulated) | ~30 m³ @ ~$10k/m³ installed | $300k |
| Cold tank (carbon steel, insulated) | ~30 m³ @ ~$5k/m³ | $150k |
| Salt-to-working-fluid HX(s) | ~1 MWth duty, exotic alloys | $150k |
| Molten-salt pumps (×2) + VFDs | specialty cantilever pumps | $200k |
| Electric trace heating (anti-freeze) | all wetted lines/valves | $75k |
| High-temp piping & valves | Ni-alloy/SS, specialty valves | $125k |
| Foundation (freeze-protected) + structural steel | | $125k |
| Instrumentation & controls (salt level, temp, PLC) | | $100k |
| Electrical/switchgear | | $65k |
| **Direct cost subtotal** | | **~$1.34M** |
| + site integration/labor (~20%) | | +$268k |
| + EPC/engineering/contingency (~35%, no scale to amortize) | | +$563k |
| **Total installed capital** | | **~$2.17M** |

**$2.17M / 5,000 kWh ≈ $430/kWh** installed — with Fermi uncertainty I'd bracket that as **$250–650/kWh**.

**Cross-check against real plants:** published 2-tank molten-salt TES costs for *utility-scale* CSP systems (hundreds to thousands of MWh_th, e.g. Andasol/Solana-class) run **$30–60/kWh_th**. Storage-tank economics roughly follow a six-tenths scaling law (cost/kWh ∝ size^-0.4). Scaling $35/kWh at ~3,000 MWh down to 5 MWh: (5/3000)^-0.4 ≈ 13×, giving **~$450/kWh** — matching the bottom-up build almost exactly. That convergence is reassuring: a 5 MWh unit is ~600× smaller than a typical commercial CSP TES loop, and tanks/pumps/trace-heating/I&C don't shrink proportionally — there's a floor cost to having two tanks, a pump skid, and a control system at all.

## Levelized cost per kWh delivered

Molten salt is sensible-heat storage, not an electrochemical cell — there's no capacity-fade "cycle life" in the battery sense; life is set by tank/pump/pipe fatigue and corrosion, typically **25–30 years**, cycled roughly daily (~7,500 cycles over the life).

- **As delivered heat** (process heat / CSP, no reconversion): thermal retention is high (~95–98%/cycle for a well-insulated small tank, though small tanks lose proportionally more surface-to-volume heat than big ones). Capital-only levelized cost:
 $2.17M / (5,000 kWh × 7,500 cycles) ≈ **$0.058/kWh_th** (~6¢/kWh, before O&M).

- **As delivered electricity** (Carnot-battery mode: resistive/heat-pump charge → steam/ORC discharge): round-trip efficiency is dominated by the power cycle, not the storage — roughly 0.98 (charge) × 0.95 (thermal retention) × ~0.37 (Rankine/ORC conversion) ≈ **33–35% round trip**.
 $2.17M / (1,650 kWh_e × 7,500 cycles) ≈ **$0.175/kWh_e** (~17–18¢/kWh, before O&M).
 Add realistic O&M (trace-heat parasitic power, pump power, salt makeup, maintenance — order 2–3%/yr of capex) and this roughly doubles, landing near **25–35¢/kWh_e**.

## Competitiveness vs lithium-ion

Current benchmarks (checked via web search, 2025): turnkey utility-scale Li-ion BESS has fallen to **~$100–165/kWh** globally (as low as $63/kWh in China, more like $150–250/kWh in the US/Europe), at round-trip efficiencies of **~90–95%**, with ~4,000–6,000 cycle life. Scaled down to a matched 5 MWh system (Li-ion is modular — containerized racks — so its small-scale penalty is much milder than tanks/pumps), a realistic installed cost is **~$250–450/kWh**: similar order of magnitude to the molten-salt build above.

That near-tie in capital $/kWh is misleading, though, because of efficiency:

- Li-ion: ~$300/kWh ÷ (6,000 cycles × ~0.9 effective RTE) ≈ **$0.056–0.09/kWh_e** delivered.
- Molten salt (round-tripped to electricity): **$0.18–0.35/kWh_e** delivered, 3–5× higher, purely because a heat engine's ~35–40% conversion efficiency is baked into every discharge.

**Verdict:** at 5 MWh, molten-salt TES is **not cost-competitive with lithium-ion for electricity storage** — the small-scale diseconomy in tanks/pumps/trace-heating erases any thermodynamic simplicity, and even where capital $/kWh roughly ties, Li-ion's far higher round-trip efficiency wins decisively on $/kWh *delivered*. Molten salt only becomes competitive in two situations: (1) scaled up by ~2–3 orders of magnitude (hundreds to thousands of MWh, as in actual CSP plants), where it drops to $30–60/kWh_th and the fixed BOP costs amortize away; or (2) used to deliver **heat directly** rather than being reconverted to electricity, since then there's no power-cycle efficiency penalty and its ~6¢/kWh_th capital-only cost is genuinely attractive against anything requiring electric resistance heating from a battery. A standalone 5 MWh molten-salt "battery" is essentially a pilot-plant-scale system chasing GWh-scale economics — it's the wrong tool at this size.

Sources:
- [Molten Salt Power Tower Cost Model for the System Advisor Model (SAM)](https://research-hub.nrel.gov/en/publications/molten-salt-power-tower-cost-model-for-the-system-advisor-model-s/)
- [Technical and Economic Feasibility of Molten Chloride Salt Thermal Energy Storage Systems](https://research-hub.nrel.gov/en/publications/technical-and-economic-feasibility-of-molten-chloride-salt-therma-2/)
- [All-in BESS projects now cost just $125/kWh as of October 2025 (Ember)](https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/how-cheap-is-battery-storage/)
- [Volta's 2025 Battery Report: Costs keep falling, boosting BESS across the globe](https://www.ess-news.com/?p=7980)
- [NREL ATB — Utility-Scale Battery Storage](https://atb.nrel.gov/electricity/2024/utility-scale_battery_storage)
